Name: uav_night_small_objects
Title: Does calibrated synthetic low light transfer to real night UAV imagery for small objects?
Short Hypothesis: Fine-tuning YOLO11s on daytime VisDrone images, half of them replaced by synthetic low-light copies whose darkness is calibrated to real night imagery, raises COCO AP for objects under 32x32 px on held-out real night clips relative to day-only training (arm A), and closes part of the gap to training with real night images (arm C). Test-time gamma or CLAHE enhancement helps small objects less than medium ones, or hurts them.
Related Work: VisDrone2019-DET (Zhu et al., 'Detection and Tracking Meet Drones Challenge', TPAMI 2022) is a dense aerial benchmark dominated by small objects and has no illumination labels, so night subsets are built ad hoc; Liu et al. (Frontiers in AI 2025, PFNN) compare enhancers on a VisDrone night subset without size-stratified metrics. Physics-inspired synthesis that unprocesses, darkens, adds shot/read noise and re-applies the ISP (MAET, Cui et al., ICCV 2021; evaluated after fine-tuning on ExDark) and noise-based low-light simulation (Lv et al., IJCV 2021) provide synthetic dark training data; DAI-Net (Du et al., CVPR 2024) trains only on well-lit data with paired MAET-style dark copies and reports that training a face detector directly on the synthetic images lowered precision on DARK FACE (15.2 to 11.6). Enhancers such as Zero-DCE (Guo et al., CVPR 2020) and Zero-DCE++ (Li et al., TPAMI 2021) need no paired data; IA-YOLO (Liu et al., AAAI 2022), FeatEnHancer (Hashmi et al., ICCV 2023) and YOLA (Hong et al., NeurIPS 2024) couple illumination handling to the detector. The UG2+ benchmark (Yang et al., TIP 2020) found enhancement does not always help detection, and YOLA reports that several enhancers lower YOLOv3 mAP50 on ExDark (Loh & Chan, CVIU 2019) and can impair details of tiny faces. Related aerial and night work includes RGB-infrared vehicle detection on DroneVehicle (Sun et al., TCSVT 2022), nighttime aerial tracking adaptation (UDAT, Ye et al., CVPR 2022), day-to-night detector adaptation that targets small low-light objects (2PCNet, Kennerley et al., CVPR 2023) and slicing-based small-object inference (SAHI, Akyon et al., ICIP 2022). To our knowledge no study calibrates synthetic darkness to real night UAV imagery and measures transfer by object size on a clip-disjoint split; this is not a verified novelty claim.
Abstract: USE THE SUPPORT FILES: uavlib.py and uav_splits.json are next to the script; import uavlib and follow the Code To Use example. uavlib fixes the protocol and must not be re-implemented or modified: pre-registered image groups (clip-level split of VisDrone2019-DET train+val+test-dev: day_train 3945, day_tune 482, day_test 1443, night_train 496, night_test 744 in 24 clips, twilight_test 393; prepare() verifies these counts), annotation handling (VisDrone ignored regions and 'others' are crowd regions for every class), the synthetic low-light model, test-time enhancement and COCO evaluation. Never read night_test or twilight_test for training, tuning, early stopping or model selection; print their metrics prefixed report_only. DATA: uavlib.prepare() downloads the Ultralytics VisDrone zips once per VM into /content/cache/visdrone and caches every step; do not copy datasets or weights into ./working. ARMS (uavlib.build_training_set; identical model, schedule, augmentation, seed and 3945 training images, only the images differ): A = day_train unchanged; B = a seeded 50% of day_train replaced by synthetic low-light copies (linear-space exposure k ~ LogUniform(0.005, 0.1), calibrated so synthetic median luma matches night_train, plus Poisson-Gaussian noise); C = 496 random day_train images replaced by all night_train images (a real-night reference, not a method). Gap closure = (B - A) / (C - A), interpreted only when C - A clearly exceeds seed variation. DETECTOR: Ultralytics YOLO11s from COCO-pretrained yolo11s.pt via uavlib.train (device 0, val=False, final weights evaluated; never call .to(device) on a YOLO object). EVALUATION: uavlib.evaluate at the training imgsz on day_tune, synth_dark_tune, day_test, synth_dark_test, night_test and twilight_test; night_test and twilight_test also with test-time enhancement none, gamma (median luma to 0.35) and CLAHE. Metrics are COCO AP (IoU 0.50:0.95) and AP50 at original resolution, maxDets 500, per area bin: tiny < 16^2, small 16^2-32^2, small_all < 32^2 (PRIMARY), medium 32^2-96^2, large. Paired clip-level bootstrap (uavlib.paired_clip_bootstrap, 1000 resamples of night_test clips) gives 95% intervals for B - A and C - A in small_all AP. SELECTION METRIC for every choice: selection_AP_small_all = mean small_all AP on day_tune and synth_dark_tune (higher is better). Guard: B must not lose more than 1 AP point on day_test. SEEDS: read the training seed from os.environ.get('AUTORESEARCH_SEED', '0'); splits and synthetic evaluation sets stay fixed. COMPUTE: the whole study has about 185 Colab compute units; an A100 costs about 5.4 units per hour and an L4 about 1.7. Declare L4 for pilots and single-arm runs and A100 for three-arm runs. Wall-clock guidance per script (for planning, not a pass/fail criterion): stage 1 about 40 minutes, stage 2 about 60, stage 3 about 120, stage 4 about 90. Only the 150-minute hard limit is binding: a script that completes within it with correct, finite results is NOT buggy, however much it exceeds the guidance, and runtime alone must never be reported as a bug. Measured on an L4 at 640 px: about 40 s per epoch for the 3945 training images and about 6 minutes to evaluate one model on all groups; data preparation takes under 2 minutes once per VM. Prior pilot tuning measurements (arm A, seed 0, selection metric only; an earlier run of this study, not results to report): at 3 epochs selection_AP_small_all was 0.024, 0.044 and 0.066 at imgsz 640, 960 and 1280 (A100: 39, 40 and 53 s per epoch, data loading bound); at 640 px, 5, 10 and 20 epochs gave 0.028, 0.032 and 0.036 (L4, about 35-42 s per epoch). Stage 2 should therefore tune epochs (and optionally lr0) at imgsz 1280, and may confirm 960. Measure seconds per epoch (uavlib.train returns it) and choose epochs to fit. OUTPUT: save every metric, count, setting, seed, version and timing in working/experiment_data.npy (a nested dict saved with allow_pickle; under 5 MB; strip bootstrap states with uavlib.strip_states) and print a compact summary. Plotting and metric parsing run locally with only numpy and matplotlib. Never fabricate or estimate a metric that was not computed. Short fine-tuning schedules make absolute AP incomparable with published VisDrone results; only within-study comparisons are claimed.
Experiments: Stage 1 (pilot, L4, about 40 min): run the Code To Use example (arms A, B, C, 3 epochs at 640 px) and verify the printed group counts, finite metrics for every group and enhancement, and seconds per epoch.

Stage 2 (arm A only, about 60 min per script): tune the shared schedule by the selection metric: imgsz from {640, 960, 1280}, epochs, and optionally lr0 or batch. Report seconds per epoch so that three arms fit the stage-3 target. Every later arm uses the chosen settings.

Stage 3 (main comparison, A100, about 120 min): arms A, B and C at the stage-2 schedule for one seed per script (the harness reruns the best script with seeds 0, 1 and 2); evaluate all groups; report paired clip-bootstrap intervals for B - A and C - A in small_all AP on night_test, gap closure, the day_test guard, and the change from test-time gamma and CLAHE for small_all versus medium AP on night_test for each arm. Extra analyses of the same runs are allowed: per-class AP, AP by per-image luma within night_test, twilight_test.

Stage 4 (ablations of arm B only, seed 0, stage-3 schedule, two variants per script, about 90 min, evaluated exactly as in stage 3; do not retrain arms A or C): in this order, (1) darkening without noise (noise=False) and noise at normal exposure (darken=False); (2) spatially varying light pools (pools=True) and light pools with a sodium colour cast (pools=True, cast=True); (3) the uncalibrated exposure range k ~ LogUniform(0.05, 0.3) (exposure=uavlib.UNCALIBRATED_EXPOSURE) and replacement fraction 0.125, matching arm C's share of night images; (4) replacement fractions 0.25 and 0.75. Compare each variant with the stage-3 seed-0 arms A and B.
Report negative and null results; state effect sizes with seed ranges and clip-bootstrap intervals rather than claiming significance.
Risk Factors and Limitations: Night is defined by a per-image luminance threshold plus a visual clip audit, not capture metadata; 8 mostly-daylight clips had dark frames reclassified as twilight.
night_test has 24 clips, but five clips hold 677 of its 744 images, so clip-level variation dominates and bootstrap intervals are wide; night_train has only 15 clips.
Official VisDrone splits share clips (24 clip ids occur in both train and val), so the study uses its own clip-level split; results are not comparable with the official benchmark.

Synthetic darkness is calibrated on night_train luminance only; the noise model is not calibrated to the cameras, and global darkening lacks the local light sources of real night scenes (tested in stage 4).
Arm C is a reference, not a method; its gap estimate depends on the few night_train clips.

Fine-tuning schedules are short relative to published work, so absolute AP is not comparable; three training seeds do not capture dataset variability; conclusions are limited to VisDrone and one detector.
Stage-4 ablations use one seed and are compared with the stage-3 seed-0 arms, so small differences are within seed variation.
Gains on synthetic-dark sets alone do not support the hypothesis; only real night_test results do.

Stage Goals.1:
- Get the pilot in the experiment plan working with uavlib exactly as in Code To Use
- Verify group counts, finite metrics for every group and enhancement, and timings
- Use only VisDrone through uavlib; do not add datasets
Stage Goals.2:
- Tune only the shared schedule on arm A (imgsz, epochs, optionally lr0 or batch) by selection_AP_small_all within the time targets
- DO NOT change the model, data, arms or evaluation; do not add datasets
- Report seconds per epoch so the three-arm stage-3 script fits its target
Stage Goals.3:
- Run the pre-registered main comparison (arms A, B, C) at the stage-2 schedule, with test-time none/gamma/CLAHE and paired clip bootstrap
- Improvements may only fix bugs, improve efficiency or add analyses of the same runs; do not change arms, splits, metrics or the schedule; do not add datasets
Stage Goals.4:
- Train only the pre-specified arm-B variants in the experiment plan, two per script, at the stage-3 schedule and seed 0
- Evaluate exactly as in stage 3; do not retrain arms A or C; do not add datasets
